body.statement: Along legal arrays with \(K=o(N^{q_d})\), determine whether the jointly normalized class \(\mathcal F_{K,d}^{\mathrm{joint}}\) admits an aggregate localized empirical-process bound, uniform over \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), whose explicit \(K\)- and logarithmic order is strictly smaller than the present \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) contribution to the endpoint risk. A positive answer must give a computable two-sided localization bound for the sum of all \(K\) marginal dual fluctuations. A negative answer must instead instantiate the rational family \(\{\mathbf P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_0\cup\Theta_1\}\) with an endpoint separation of the corresponding order, \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge0\) against every rematching column, with strict slack off the declared contact columns. The currently defined search template is not asserted to establish either answer.
body.justification: The remaining upper-side issue is precisely whether aggregate localization across all jointly conjugate potentials improves \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\).
body.gap: Neither a sharper aggregate theorem nor a simultaneous all-rematching lower certificate is currently established.
body.consumer: Its answer determines which side of the small-arm risk sandwich must move.

obligation.what_is_open: For \(K=o(N^{q_d})\), either prove a computable aggregate localized complexity bound strictly sharper than \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\), with explicit logarithms, or construct the matching simultaneous finite-support family with \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\) and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge0\) for every rematching column.
obligation.obstruction: The optimal-sum diameter controls support geometry but not the sum of \(K\) marginal dual sensitivities. Fixed-dimensional orthogonal tensoring saturates after at most \(d\) directions, and no declared family has an all-column reduced-cost certificate.
obligation.attempted: Subset exchanges and common-support interpolation prove the present upper bound. Hypercube parity, orthogonal, Bernoulli-knot, and two-margin constructions certify boundary cases but do not accumulate the required growing-\(K\) separation.
obligation.partial_result:
The established common-support interpolation inequality is
\[
\left|\frac{V(\mathbf Q)-V(\mathbf P)}{K^2}\right|
\le \frac1{K^2}\left|\sum_k\int\|x\|_2^2\,d(Q_k-P_k)\right|
+\sum_k\sup_{g\in\mathcal C_{2(2\sqrt d+1)/K^2}}
\left|\int g\,d(Q_k-P_k)\right|.
\]
Together with the optimal-sum diameter \(2\sqrt r\), it gives the computable uniform upper contribution \(C_d\{N^{-1/2}+\min(r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d})\}\). It does not prove that the aggregate dual fluctuation is smaller than \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\), and it supplies no simultaneous indistinguishable family.
